rule: at most 3 single-hypothesis briefs; only mathematically live, exactly-scoped targets with a concrete decisive route

proposals.title: Refutation of Conjecture 8.8 (Cayley-avoidance maximum inequality) of Cerbai-Claesson-Ernst-Golab
proposals.exact_statement: Conjecture 8.8 (arXiv:2407.19583v1, Sec. 8; published Australas. J. Combin. 94(2) (2025) 267-299), under the section preamble 'Let p and q be two Cayley permutations of the same length': if max(p) <= max(q), then |Cay_n(p)| >= |Cay_n(q)|. Cayley permutations are words w of positive integers with letter set [1..max(w)]; w contains pattern p if some subsequence (indices nondecreasing allowed, i.e. i_1<=...<=i_k) is order-isomorphic to p (ties preserved); Cay_n(p) = p-avoiding Cayley permutations of size n (length n). Quantifiers: for all same-length pairs p,q with max(p)<=max(q) and all n.
proposals.counterexample: p=1122, q=1112 (same length 4, max(p)=max(q)=2): |Cay_5(p)|=520 < 522=|Cay_5(q)|. Persisting: n=6 gives 4340 < 4394. The negation is existentially quantified, so these two patterns plus n=5 are a COMPLETE certificate.
proposals.verification: Two independent exact implementations (scripts/decisive_cayley.py; scripts/verify_cayley_indep.py) under the pinned helper guard (512MiB AS/group-RSS, 210 CPU s / 230 wall, single-thread). Machinery cross-validated against the source's own results: |Cay_n(112)|=|Cay_n(122)|=(n+1)!/2 for n=2..6, and the source's check |Cay_n(13442)|=|Cay_n(14233)| (n<=7) reproduced; totals equal Fubini numbers. Work files: work/decisive-cayley-sweep.json, work/decisive-cayley-verify.json, work/decisive-cayley-validation.json.

primary_source.published: Australas. J. Combin. 94(2) (2025) 267-299, https://ajc.maths.uq.edu.au/pdf/94/ajc_v94_p267.pdf (Conjecture 8.8 verified verbatim on p.30; conjecture is the last item before references; no resolution)

proposals.closest_predecessor: Conjectures 8.5-8.7 of the same paper (same section); Jelinek-Mansour word-equivalence results; the paper's own content-multiplicity non-equivalence witness 13442/14233 for Conjecture 8.6.
proposals.closest_successor: Cerbai-Claesson, 'Counting fixed-point-free Cayley permutations' (arXiv:2507.09304) and the 2026 Hertzsprung-patterns-in-Cayley-permutations paper (akc.is/papers/054) are the only follow-ups found; neither addresses Conjecture 8.8. No public refutation found (searched 2026-10-30).
proposals.scope_comparison: Early actual-scope check done: same-length restriction honored (both patterns length 4); ties handled per the source's definition (verified via the source's own 112 formula); the record's 'for every relevant size n' matches the source's implicit all-n quantifier.
proposals.expected_certificate_size: 2 patterns + n + two integers (520, 522); replay = enumeration of the 541 Cayley words of size 5 (sub-second); independent re-derivation by any exact word enumerator.
proposals.formalization_dependencies: Finite lists/nat words; decidable subsequence rank-type predicate; counting over an explicit finite set. Lean endpoint needs no axioms beyond standard (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound allowed); no analysis.
proposals.prior_subsumption_objections: (1) The published AJC version (checked) retains the conjecture unresolved - chronology favors novelty; (2) the source authors verified 8.6's candidate to n<=9 for a different pair, so their tooling plausibly could have found ours - but no published statement of it exists; (3) if the authors intended an unstated restriction (e.g., patterns with all letters distinct), the certificate would not apply - the verbatim published statement has no such restriction.
proposals.status: counterexample complete and verified in-lane; needs independent adversarial review + published-chronology double-check before credit; root assigns review separately.
